newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No breakthrough in Israel-PLO meeting - negotiator.
newsitem.headline: No breakthrough in Israel-PLO meeting - negotiator.

text.p: A senior PLO negotiator said on Thursday after a U.S.-sponsored meeting with Israel's defence minister that Middle East peace efforts were still in deep crisis.

"I realise now the magnitude of the crisis," Palestinian cabinet minister Saeb Erekat said after Wednesday's late-night session at the residence near Tel Aviv of U.S. ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk. "We are still in a major, major crisis."

Erekat and Palestinian Planning and International Cooperation Minister Nabil Shaath met for three hours with Israeli defence chief Yitzhak Mordechai and Yitzhak Molcho, an adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The meeting, initiated and attended by U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, was aimed at exploring the chances of resuming formal peace negotiations broken off in March after Israel began building a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem.

"It was a very candid meeting, right to the point. There were no clear-cut results," Erekat said. "Ross will continue from here with the leaders. He will see both (Palestinian President Yasser) Arafat and Netanyahu tomorrow (Thursday)."

Erekat told Reuters in a telephone interview that the Palestinian side raised the issues of Jerusalem, Israeli land confiscation and settlement activities. The PLO has demanded Israel halt settlement work before peace talks can resume.

"We still insist that if there is no freeze on settlement activities, including Jabal Abu Ghneim, there will be no restoration of the credibility of the peace process," he said, referring to the site of the Israeli building project.
Israeli officials were not immediately available for comment.
But Erekat said the Israeli side raised the issue of "fighting terrorism".

Netanyahu has insisted that before peace talks resume Arafat must crack down on Moslem militants. Two months ago, an Islamic bomber killed himself and three Israeli women in a blast at a Tel Aviv cafe.

"Tonight's meeting was simply a dialogue. It was not negotiations nor a restoration of negotiations. The Americans listened and before Ross leaves (the region) on Friday he will take up the issues with the leaders," Erekat said.
A PLO official, who asked not to be identified, said no date was set for another Israeli-Palestinian meeting.
Israeli leaders have said they will not stop work at the East Jerusalem site they call Har Homa, insisting Jews have a right to live in all the biblical Land of Israel, which includes the West Bank.
Israel annexed East Jerusalem and declared all the city its eternal and indivisible capital after the 1967 Middle East war. The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy was due to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington on Friday.
Before Wednesday's Israel-PLO meeting, Levy said he hoped for a quick resumption of bilateral talks on implementing peace deals.
